title: Finite affine-cover alternating totalization of a quasi-coherent resolution
statement: Let $X$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], $r\geq0$, and $U:\operatorname{Fin}(r)\to X_{\mathrm{open}}$ a family with $\bigcup_i U_i=X$. Suppose every intersection indexed by a nonempty tuple, allowing repetitions and empty opens, is affine. Let $F,J$ be unbounded cochain complexes of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], every term of $F$ quasi-coherent [pqf-def-coherent], and $J$ K-injective [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. For every quasi-isomorphism $i:F\to J$, the morphism $T_U(i):T_U(F)\to T_U(J)$ of the actual alternating total functor [def-sc-alternating-cech-total-complex] is a quasi-isomorphism. This assertion is about a specified cochain map, without localization or comparison-map data.

source.place: Cohomology, Lemma 08C2, affine-basis case using Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 01XB; parent proof Steps 2--3

proof.text: Apply affineOpenSections_resolution_quasiIso to each increasing tuple intersection. No cover hypothesis is needed for this component.

Construct the projection chain maps from an actual nonnegative column to the section complexes. Their product is an isomorphism: degreewise use extensionXIso, ModuleCat.piIsoPi, and the evaluation product comparison. Finite products of section quasi-isomorphisms are quasi-isomorphisms because the additive homology functor preserves finite products. Naturality of the projections transports this result to the actual column map.

Negative columns vanish by extension by zero. Columns p at least r vanish since an injection Fin(p+1) into Fin r would imply p+1 <= r. Thus both double complexes are strictly supported from 0 through r-1. Apply the existing finite-column total comparison theorem. This includes r=0 with an empty interval.

proof_origin.place: Tag 08C2 affine intersections; T1 explicit product projection chain maps and finite column bounds, then existing finite-column comparison theorem.
